memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Moses answered them, "Wait until I find out what the Lord commands concerning you." Then the Lord said to Moses, "Tell the Israelites: 'When any of you or your descendants are unclean because of a dead body or are away on a journey, they are still to celebrate the Lord's Passover, but they are to do it on the fourteenth day of the second month at twilight.'" - Num 9:8-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Faced with the men's honest question, Moses did something wise: he did not rush to answer on his own. He said, "Wait until I find out what the Lord commands." He brought the matter to God. And God graciously responded with a provision — a "second Passover" a month later, so that those who could not keep it at the normal time would not miss out.

What a picture of the heart of God. He did not say, "Rules are rules; too bad for them." Instead, He made a way for the excluded to be included. His grace opened a door where circumstances had closed one.

This tells us something precious about God's character, which never changes: He is a God of mercy who makes a way for those who long to come to Him. He is not looking for reasons to shut people out, but for ways to welcome them in.

There is also wisdom in Moses' example. When we face a hard question and do not know the answer, the best response is not to invent one, but to bring it to God and wait on Him. "If any of you lacks wisdom, you should ask God, who gives generously" (Jas 1:5).

The second Passover reminds us that God's mercy reaches those who feel they have missed their chance. In Christ, God has made the ultimate way for all who were once excluded to be brought near (Eph 2:13). No one who truly seeks Him is left without a way home.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you bring your hard questions to God and wait on Him?
- How does God's "second Passover" reveal His merciful heart?
- Have you felt you "missed your chance"? What does this passage say?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You are a God who makes a way for those who long to come to You. Teach me to wait on You for wisdom, and to trust Your mercy. Amen.
